## PR Description

Closes #865
### Root Cause
- The gh-857/863 in-place placeholder conclusion detects ghosts only via `placeholders()`/`headPlaceholders()`, which requires a PENDING check-run with NO numeric run id (`isPlaceholderShape`).
- Live fa #1457 head fd1b9aa2: GitHub minted in_progress pseudo-job check-runs WITH run ids on the kicker suite (run 38164305157, concluded success) after the ~10-13 min speculative window expired — the detector skipped them, `classify()` only offered the same-sha re-dispatch, and the checks pinned `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` for 4+ hours with every real check green.

### Previous Attempt
- #863 (gh-857 in-place conclusion) fixed the no-numeric-id variant; insufficient because its detector required the ABSENCE of a run id, and these orphans have ids plus a completed owning run.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js`: new pure detector `orphanedRunChecks()` — the generalized orphan rule: a pending check-run whose OWNING RUN has concluded (any conclusion, past the propagation grace) is definitionally orphaned. Disjoint from the other detectors: no-run-id → gh-852 placeholder detector; owning run absent → classify `no-run` zombie (keeps the re-dispatch remedy); owning run active → AC2 untouched.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new probe `headOrphanedRunChecks()` (same transport contract: null = probe degraded); the gh-857 conclude gate now concludes placeholders AND orphans in one pass (`phTargets`), keeping both fail-safes — real completed-success green cover required (AC3 verdict mirror), no active run on the head (AC2). The gh-852 fresh-sha reset stays keyed on link-less placeholders only; orphan-only heads that cannot conclude fall through to the legacy same-sha dispatch.

### Test Coverage
- `test_checkRunZombies.js`: 10 new `orphanedRunChecks` tests (fd1b9aa2 replay, 3-item multi-orphan, live/cancelled/absent/grace/probe-error/settled/link-less negatives, grace knob) — RED before, GREEN after.
- `test_smAgent.js`: 2 new `validate_pr` tests — green head + 3 numeric-id orphans → exactly 3 `PATCH` conclusions mirroring the green run, no reset, no re-dispatch; owning run still in_progress → zero PATCHes (AC2). RED before the wiring (verified via stash), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2595 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- Orphan conclusion mirrors the head's green verdict only — a cancelled/failed owning run never produces a green conclusion without a real green cover on the head.
- The optional second layer (dispatch validation promptly for reworked heads) is intentionally not implemented — the conclude step is the agreed safety net.

# gh-865: [BUG] Placeholder conclude misses numeric-id orphans: in_progress check-runs on CONCLUDED suites still pin required contexts (fa #1457 saga root cause)

## Description

Follow-up to #848 / #863 (which fixed the no-numeric-id placeholder variant). Full evidence: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/848#issuecomment-6114638294

**Live failure (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, 2026-10-11, still BLOCKED):** run 38164305157 (push-triggered kicker workflow) completed/success at 18:33:24, yet its suite 103398997480 carries three pseudo-job check-runs stuck in_progress for 4+ hours: `Quality gate` (114566277295), `JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)` (114566278905), `Binaries smoke gate` (114566280823). GitHub evaluates these placeholders for the required contexts → mergeStateStatus BLOCKED despite 4 green CI runs and repeated SM bridge-free success stamps on the same head.

**Root race:** rework push → kicker suite created instantly → SM dispatches CI only on its next tick (here +18 min) → GitHub's ~10-13 min speculative-placeholder window expires with no required-context stamps → placeholders minted ON THE KICKER'S SUITE with numeric run ids.

**Why #863's conclude misses them:** the detector keys on placeholders lacking numeric run ids; these have ids and a completed owning run.

**Required fix — generalized orphan rule:** an in_progress check-run whose OWNING RUN has concluded (any conclusion) is definitionally orphaned → conclude it with the mirrored verdict, keeping the existing fail-safe (never conclude while a live run covers that head/context). This subsumes both variants.

**Prevention (optional, second layer):** shrink the race window — dispatch validation for reworked approved heads promptly (or have the kicker itself defer its suite), so required contexts are stamped before the ~10-13 min placeholder window closes. The conclude step stays the safety net.

**Acceptance:** on fa #1457's current head (or a synthetic reproduction: kicker suite + no required stamps for >13 min), a tick concludes the orphaned placeholders and mergeStateStatus flips from BLOCKED. Unit test: in_progress check-run + completed owning run + mirror verdict present → PATCH completed; owning run still in_progress → untouched.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

If vOrphans is null, `(vOrphans && vOrphans.length)` is false. So entry into the block means vPh non-empty OR vOrphans non-empty. Case A: vPh non-empty (array) → concat fine. Case B: vPh null/empty and vOrphans non-empty — can vPh be null while vOrphans is non-empty? headPlaceholders returns null only when checkRuns === null; headOrphanedRunChecks returns null when checkRuns === null OR runs === null. If checkRuns probe failed, both null → block not entered. If checkRuns succeeded, vPh is an array (maybe empty) → concat fine. But could checkRuns probe succeed in headPlaceholders and fail in headOrphanedRunChecks? Two separate calls to headCheckRunsSafe — yes! First call could succeed, second call could fail (transient). The outer catch swallows it so it fails safe (retry next tick), but it aborts the entire validate_pr action for that ticket — including skipping dispatch. The zombie sweep at line ~2763 (rcHeadRuns / hasActiveHeadRun) etc. Not critical.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `vPh.concat` null-deref when the two probes disagree**

The outer gate at line 2365 enters this block when **either** detector fires, but `vPh` can be `null` here while `vOrphans` is a non-empty array:

- `headPlaceholders()` returns `null` only when its `headCheckRunsSafe()` fetch throws — but that is a **separate** `github_get_commit_check_runs` API call from the one inside `headOrphanedRunChecks()`. A transient failure (rate-limit hiccup, 5xx) on the first call and success on the second is entirely possible.
- In that case `(vPh && vPh.length)` is falsy, `(vOrphans && vOrphans.length)` is truthy, the block is entered, and line 2400 does `null.concat(...)` → TypeError.

The action-level `catch` in `validate_pr` swallows it, so the PR is only skipped for one tick (fail-safe, self-heals) — but it aborts the whole validate_pr action for that PR, which is exactly the "probe degraded → keep legacy behavior" case the module docs say should degrade gracefully.

One-line fix:

```javascript
var phTargets = (vPh || []).concat(vOrphans || []);
```

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `orphanedRunChecks()` re-implements `classify()`'s run-linked branch**

The resolve → absent / active / completed → parse `updated_at` → grace-window sequence here (~lines 286–297) is nearly line-for-line the logic in `classify()` (lines 146–173). The detectors are deliberately disjoint in their *verdicts* (classify splits `cancelled` vs `run-concluded`; orphans lump any conclusion) — but the *transport* semantics (absent ⇒ skip, throw ⇒ fail safe, grace ⇒ still landing) are identical and will drift the next time one is tuned.

Consider extracting a shared helper, e.g. `resolveRunState(runId, resolveRun, nowMs, graceMs)` returning a normalized verdict (`'absent' | 'active' | 'in-grace' | {conclusion, endedMs}`), with `classify()` and `orphanedRunChecks()` both consuming it. Not blocking — the duplication is acknowledged and tested on both sides today.

Review complete. **Verdict: APPROVE** (0 blocking · 1 important · 2 suggestions).

## Summary

**Reviewed:** full PR diff (via `git diff origin/main...HEAD` — `pr_diff.txt` was truncated), the complete `checkRunZombies.js`, the validate_pr conclude/reset flow and probe plumbing in `smAgent.js`, both new test suites, AGENTS.md conventions (GraalJS `var`-only — new code complies), plus a local full-suite run: **2595 passed, 0 failed** (confirms the PR claim).

**Findings:**

1. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — `js/smAgent.js:2400`: `vPh.concat(vOrphans || [])` can throw a TypeError. The outer gate enters when *either* detector fires, but `headPlaceholders()` and `headOrphanedRunChecks()` make **independent** check-runs API calls — a transient failure on the first and success on the second leaves `vPh === null` with a non-empty `vOrphans`. The action-level catch makes it fail-safe (one skipped tick), but it violates the documented "probe degraded → keep legacy behavior" contract. Fix: `(vPh || []).concat(vOrphans || [])`.

2. 💡 **SUGGESTION** — `js/smAgent.js:2364`: the check-runs list is fetched twice per validate_pr evaluation (both probes hit the same endpoint back-to-back, run rollup refetched again at line 2390), doubling GitHub API traffic per tick per PR. Fetch once, pass the array into both pure detectors — this also structurally eliminates finding 1.

3. 💡 **SUGGESTION** — `js/common/checkRunZombies.js:277`: `orphanedRunChecks()` re-implements `classify()`'s run-linked branch (resolve → absent/active/completed → grace) nearly line-for-line; verdicts differ by design but the transport semantics will drift. Extract a shared `resolveRunState` helper.

**Verified:** ticket ACs met (fd1b9aa2 replay + 3-item multi-orphan → PATCH with mirrored verdict; owning run in_progress → zero PATCHes), gh-852 reset budget untouched for orphan-only heads, detectors provably disjoint, no security/backward-compat concerns (token-swap pattern pre-existing, exports only extended).

**Artifacts:** `outputs/pr_review.json` (APPROVE), `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` … `comment3.md`.
